Let's recall history only for Up and Down without Shift, Ctrl, Alt or

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep edits to recalled commands while browsing

Only the text typed before recalling is saved. A TA who edits a

Let's keep the text left at each history position until the next
command is entered, so moving away and back restores the edit. The
history itself still keeps each command as it was entered.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore whitespace-only input in the command box
commitResults.messageBody:

and adds it to the command history, so Up can recall a blank entry.

Let's treat whitespace-only input like an empty box: nothing runs and
nothing is added to the history.

Let's check that the typed text and a recalled command keep their
edits separately, and that Up and Down with each modifier leave the
text alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject fractional marks in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A hand-edited participation score or grade such as 5.9 loads as 5,
and the next save writes the truncated value back. The UG requires
whole numbers, and an invalid file should be protected, not changed.

Let's make the JSON reader reject fractional numbers in whole-number
fields, so such a file fails to load and stays untouched.

Fixes #132

Let's parse exit the same way, so extra input shows the usual

Fixes #136

commitResults.messageTitle: Limit whole-number check to marks in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:

instead of the whole-number message the UG describes.

toModelType() instead, with the existing whole-number messages. A mark
with a zero fractional part, such as 5.0, is read as a whole number,
so a hand edit that keeps the .0 still loads.

Update the DG to say fractional marks are rejected on load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Hash assignment names consistently with equality
commitResults.messageBody:

lowercased name. Names such as "PSI" and "psı" (dotless i) are equal
but have different hash codes, so a hand-edited data file can hold two
records for the same assignment and student, and one grade silently
replaces the other.

Let's move GroupName's case-folding hash into StringUtil and use it
for both names, so equal names always hash alike and the duplicate
record is rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show why the data file was rejected at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
When the saved file cannot be loaded, the app shows only that the data
could not be read. The reason, such as two students sharing an ID, is
written only to the log file, which a TA is unlikely to open, so a bad
manual edit is hard to repair.

Let's include the reason in the startup message. Invalid data gives its
own message, a JSON syntax error or a value of the wrong type names the
line where reading stopped, and any other read error says the file
could not be opened. DataLoadStatus becomes a small class so a failed
status can carry this reason.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the load-failure reason without a location
commitResults.messageBody:
Codecov reports the no-location branch of the reason as untested, and
DataLoadStatus has an unused toString and an equals check that cannot
differ.

Let's test a JSON error with no location, drop toString, and compare
statuses by message alone, since each message belongs to one outcome.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject data commands after a failed load
commitResults.messageBody:
When the saved data cannot be read at startup, TAssist starts with no
data and blocks saving. Listing commands still run on the empty data,
so group list suggests group add, which is then rejected, and student
list asks the TA to create or select a group.

Let's reject every command except help, view and exit with the
existing recovery message while the saved data is unreadable, so the
TA is told to repair the file instead of being sent in circles.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report a missing space before a prefix
commitResults.messageBody:
A prefix only starts a parameter at the start of input or after a
space. When the TA leaves out that space, as in id/A0123456Xw/3, the
prefix becomes part of the previous value, and TAssist reports w/ as
missing even though the TA typed it.

Let's check whether a missing prefix appears inside another value
right after other text, and if so report the missing space before it
instead, so the TA knows what to fix.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reword the recovery message for listing commands
commitResults.messageBody:
After a failed load, listing commands such as group list also get the
recovery message, but it ends with "restart before making changes",
which reads oddly when the TA only wanted to see their records.

Let's end it with "restart to see or change your records" instead, and
rewrap a Developer Guide line that grew past the usual width.

commitResults.messageTitle: Hint at a missing space after a spaced word too
commitResults.messageBody:
The missing-space error quotes the whole value, so a value with many
words makes a long message. When the joined word follows a space, as
in n/Alice Tanid/A1, TAssist reports only the unknown prefix Tanid/,
which hides the real typo.

Let's quote only the value's first word, the only word that can hide
a prefix, and add "If id/ starts a new parameter, put a space before
it." to an unknown prefix that ends with an allowed prefix the input
lacks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save a group rename that only changes case
commitResults.messageBody:
A rename such as T01 to t01 reports success, but the change is never
saved, and undo skips it and reverses the command before it. Logic
saves and records undo history only if the data before and after the
command differ, and group equality ignores the name's case.

Let's make Group#equals compare the name's exact capitalization, so a
case-only rename is saved and undone like any other change. Lookups
and duplicate checks still ignore case.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the spacing hint only after another value
commitResults.messageBody:
The hint for an unknown prefix that ends with an allowed one also
appears for a mistyped prefix name, such as status/ or studentid/,
and for a first word such as T01g/, where adding the space does not
help.

Let's add the hint only when the word follows another value and the
text before the allowed prefix is not all lowercase letters, so that
n/Alice Tanid/A1 keeps it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check for a missing space in group commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The group parsers report their own missing names, so a name typed
right after another value without a space, as in group rename
g/T01n/T02, says the name is missing or invalid.

Let's run the same missing-space check there as the student parsers
do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report unchanged updates and show replaced grades
commitResults.messageBody:
Repeating a submission status, grade, group rename, or group use says
the value was updated, although nothing changed and nothing is saved.
Replacing a grade also hides the grade that was overwritten.

Let's report "Nothing changed." for these repeats, as attendance and
participation do, and show the old and new grade when one is replaced.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: move s/no grade note to assignment submit
commitResults.messageBody:
The assignment grade section says entering s/no clears a grade, but
assignment grade has no s/ prefix and rejects it. The behavior belongs
to assignment submit.

Let's describe it in the assignment submit section and drop it from
the assignment grade section.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept a data file with a UTF-8 byte-order mark
commitResults.messageBody:
Editors such as Windows Notepad can save the data file as UTF-8 with a
byte-order mark. TAssist rejects such a file as a JSON syntax error on
line 1, even though its content is unchanged, and then blocks every
change for the session.

Let's drop a leading byte-order mark before parsing the JSON, so the
file loads as usual. The next save writes it without the mark.

commitResults.messageTitle: Repeat the load-failure reason when rejecting
commitResults.messageBody:
A command rejected after a failed load replaces the startup message
with the generic "Saved data could not be read.", so the TA can no
longer see what is wrong with the file.

Let's build the rejection from the startup message, reason included,
followed by how to recover.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG for assignment records and group export
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG's storage text and diagrams show only groups and students, and
the model diagrams leave out assignments or their records. A new
developer cannot see where submissions and grades are stored, saved
and loaded. The registration text also leaves out `group export`.

Let's add Assignment, AssignmentRecord and

diagrams, and list `export` with the group commands.

commitResults.messageBody:
Two copies started from the same home folder each save their own
copy of the data, so one copy silently overwrites changes the other
reported as saved.

Let's list this in the UG's Known issues, with how to avoid it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show help topics in the order help accepts them
commitResults.messageBody:
The Help screen listed feature commands in alphabetical order of their
keywords: attendance, group, participation, then student. help TOPIC
and the User Guide use the order group, student, attendance,
participation, so the reference read in a different order from both.

Let's group feature commands by topic in the order of the help topics.

commitResults.messageTitle: List each topic's commands in the order they are used
commitResults.messageBody:
Within a topic, help listed commands alphabetically, so student delete
came before student list and attendance list before attendance mark.
The User Guide describes them in the order a TA uses them.

Let's keep help entries in registration order, and register each
feature's commands in that order: create or record first, then list,
then delete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the help text of the built-in commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The help entry still said help shows only one topic, although help
TOPIC now opens the reference at that topic. The general commands were
also headed "Current commands", a leftover from the contact commands.

Let's describe help, view and exit as they behave now, list the help
topics, and head the general commands "General commands".

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete the help for group and student commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The group help did not give the naming rules, and its group use example
switched to T02, which the examples never create. The student delete
example removed Alice Tan, whom the attendance and participation
examples go on to use.

Let's state the rules of each command, and give examples that work
when typed in order: create T01 and T02, switch back to T01, add two
students, and delete only the second.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete the help for attendance and participation
commitResults.messageBody:
The attendance help did not say that IDs and statuses ignore case, or
what attendance list shows when no one has a mark that week. Weeks were
written as "week 1-13" in one place and "a week from 1 to 13" in
another.

Let's state these rules as the User Guide does, in the same words for
both features.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check that every help example works when typed
commitResults.messageBody:
The help promises examples a TA can type, but nothing checked that
they run, so an example could fail without anyone noticing.

Let's test the running app's help: it lists every command in help
order, each example runs its own command, and typing every example in
order into a new TAssist succeeds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the User Guide and help agree
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide described the student commands after attendance and
participation, while help lists them right after the group commands.
Several help examples, such as group add g/T02 and the student delete
example, did not appear in the guide at all.

Let's order the guide's sections as help does, show every help example
in the guide, explain how the Help screen is ordered, and test that the
guide shows every help format and example.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain how help is ordered and checked in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
Developers adding commands, such as the assignment commands, need to
know where their help appears, what makes a good example, and which
test will fail if help and the User Guide disagree.

Let's describe the order of the reference and the rules for help text,
with a class diagram of how help entries reach the Help screen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a TAssist icon for the app window
commitResults.messageBody:
The window and task bar show AddressBook's icon, which is not ours and
does not match TAssist.

Let's draw a TAssist icon, a white T with a check mark on the app's
teal, and use it in 32 and 256 pixel sizes so that the platform can
pick a sharp one. Let's remove the AddressBook icon and its entry in
copyright.txt, and credit the new icon there.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the TAssist icon in the macOS Dock
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX window icons do not reach the macOS Dock, which keeps showing
the Java icon. Windows and Linux take the task bar icon from the
window, so only macOS is affected.

Let's also set the icon through the Java platform's Taskbar where it
supports icon images. Where it does not, or the image cannot be read,
log it and carry on, as the icon is not essential.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that a mark replaces only that student's week
commitResults.messageBody:
The help said marking or setting "the same week again" replaces the
earlier record, which can be read as a later week 3 mark replacing
another student's week 3 mark.

Let's say "the same student and week", as the User Guide does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the User Guide samples to the help session
commitResults.messageBody:
After the help examples delete Ben Lim, the attendance and
participation list samples still showed him as Not recorded. The
command summary also kept group use g/T02 and the old student delete
example, which no longer follow on from the other examples.

Let's show only Alice Tan in those samples, use the help examples in
the command summary, and test that the summary uses only help
examples.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep starting if the Dock icon cannot be set
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskbarIcon caught only some of the exceptions that setting the icon
can throw. On macOS, a failure to set the Dock icon arrives as a plain
RuntimeException, and UiManager calls TaskbarIcon outside its own
error handling, so such a failure would stop TAssist from starting.

Let's catch any RuntimeException there, log it, and carry on without
the Dock icon.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read the Dock icon before checking platform support
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskbarIcon returned as soon as the platform did not support task bar
icons, before looking at the image. On headless CI that is always the
case, so the tests for a missing or unreadable image passed without
ever reading it.

Let's read the image first, in its own method, and test that method
directly with the real icon, a missing file and a file that is not an
image.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app
commitResults.messageBody:
Java disables assertions by default, so the assert statements in the
code are never checked when the app is launched with `./gradlew run`.

Let's enable assertions for the run task, so that a broken assumption
stops the app during development instead of passing silently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test a TA's whole session end to end
commitResults.messageBody:
Each feature has its own tests, but nothing checks a TA's session as a
whole: record a tutorial in every feature, close TAssist, and find
everything back. The acceptance pass needs this walkthrough, and it
should keep passing after later changes.

Let's walk through a first launch, a tutorial that uses every
feature, a restart, rejected input, a deletion and an unreadable data
file, each time through the real parsers, model and JSON storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Launch the JAR from a terminal in the DG's manual tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual tests told testers to double-click the JAR, which does not
work on every system, while the User Guide and the course ask for
java -jar. The launch section also kept AB3's "more test cases"
placeholder.

Let's launch from a terminal with Java 25, check where TAssist writes
its files, replace the placeholder with a shutdown test, and say what
each step should show.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an end-to-end acceptance walkthrough to the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG's manual tests check one feature at a time, so a tester has no
script for the usage scenario as a whole: a tutorial recorded in every
feature, a restart, mistakes, a deletion and different window sizes.

Let's write that walkthrough with the expected result of each step. It
follows the same session as AcceptanceWalkthroughTest, and adds the
checks only a person running the JAR can make.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the assignment list sample to the help session
commitResults.messageBody:
The help examples delete Ben Lim and record a grade of 87 for Alice
Tan, but the User Guide's assignment list sample still showed both
students as not submitted. The help test also skipped the assignment
topic when checking that each example runs its own command.

Let's show the listing that the examples lead to, and check every
help topic in that test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Start even when the log file cannot be written
commitResults.messageBody:
In a folder TAssist cannot write to, such as a read-only download
folder, creating the log file fails. LogsCenter then warned through
its own logger, which does not exist yet at that point, so TAssist
crashed at startup with an ExceptionInInitializerError instead of
opening.

Let's warn through the logger being set up, and carry on logging to
the console only. TAssist then opens, and a command that changes data
reports that it cannot save, as the User Guide describes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note launch and read-only folder issues in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
Testers and users may double-click the JAR, which does not work on
every system, or run it from a folder they cannot write to, where
TAssist opens but cannot save. The User Guide did not mention either.

Let's describe both in the known issues, with what TAssist shows and
how to fix it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a utility to format CSV that spreadsheets open
commitResults.messageBody:
Exporting a group's records needs CSV that Excel, Numbers and Google
Sheets all read the same way. Names can contain apostrophes, and a
value that starts with = or - would be run as a formula when the file
is opened.

Let's format rows as RFC 4180 describes: CRLF line ends, and quotes
only around fields that need them. Values that look like formulas get
an apostrophe so that spreadsheets show them as text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share how stored attendance is shown
commitResults.messageBody:
attendance list turned stored values such as PRESENT into Present in
a private method. The CSV export needs the same wording, and a second
copy of the rule could drift from the first.

Let's move the rule to AttendanceStatus and use it from attendance
list. The listing does not change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Lay out a group's records as a CSV table
commitResults.messageBody:
The CSV export needs one table per group that a course coordinator can
read without TAssist: who each student is, and their attendance and
participation in every week of the term.

Let's lay out one row per student in roster order, with the name, the
student ID, then attendance and participation for weeks 1 to 13. A
week without a record is left empty rather than given a made-up value.

commitResults.messageTitle: Write a group's records to a CSV file
commitResults.messageBody:
The table needs to reach a file that a TA can find and send on.
Excel shows accented names wrongly unless the file says it is UTF-8,
and a failed write should not leave half a file behind.

Let's write the table to <group>-records.csv in an exports folder,
with a byte order mark, through a temporary file that replaces any
earlier export of the group only once it is complete. Spaces in group
names become hyphens, so file names need no quoting.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a command that exports the active group
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors keep a copy of their group's records in a spreadsheet, for
example to hand marks to the module coordinator. TAssist can lay out
and write those records but nothing lets the user ask for it.

Let's add GroupExportCommand, which writes the active group's records
through GroupRecordsCsvExporter and shows where the file went. Export
only reads the model, so a failed write leaves the data unchanged and
reports which file could not be written.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse the group export command
commitResults.messageBody:
The export command needs a parser before it can be typed. Like
group list, it takes no parameters, so extra input is rejected with the
same message instead of being ignored.

The parser holds the exporter so that every command it creates writes
to the same folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let users type group export
commitResults.messageBody:
The export command and its parser exist, but no command word reaches
them and help does not mention them.

Let's register group export with a help entry, and document it in the
User Guide. The JAR writes exports to an exports folder next to it, like
its other files. Apps opened on another data file export beside that
file, so tests never write next to the build.

Assignment grades are left out of the file. They are kept per
assignment rather than per week, so they do not fit the week columns.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep export file names of different groups apart
commitResults.messageBody:
Spaces in a group name became hyphens in the export file name. Group
names may also contain hyphens, so Lab 1 and Lab-1 shared one file, and
exporting either group replaced the other's records.

Let's use underscores instead. Group names cannot contain them, so
each group gets its own file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain group export in the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Developers extending the export need to know where its classes sit,
where the file goes, and why it is written the way it is.

Let's describe the classes and add a sequence diagram of the command.
Let's also record why the table is wide, why the folder is fixed, and
why assignments are left out. UC09 now matches the command, and the
manual tests cover a normal export, a replaced file, an empty group,
and a failed write.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give exported files the usual permissions
commitResults.messageBody:
Running the JAR showed that exported files could be read only by their
owner. Files.createTempFile makes the temporary file private, and the
move over the export keeps those permissions. A TA who copies the file
to a shared drive or another account would then get a file others
cannot open.

Let's write to a plain temporary file named after the export instead.
It gets the same permissions as any other file in the folder, and a
temporary file left by an earlier crash is simply overwritten.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Point code links to the team repository
commitResults.messageBody:
The links to Main, MainApp, Ui, MainWindow, Logic, Model and Storage
go to the AB3 repository, so readers see AB3's code instead of
TAssist's.

Let's point them to the same files in the team repository.

commitResults.messageTitle: DevOps: Point the MainApp link to the team repository
commitResults.messageBody:
The release steps link MainApp.java in the AB3 repository, so a
developer updating the version number would open AB3's file instead
of TAssist's.

Let's point it to the same file in the team repository.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Mention the delete confirmation in manual testing
commitResults.messageBody:
The "Removing a student" step does not mention the confirmation
dialog. Cancel is selected by default, so a tester who presses Enter
cancels the deletion and the step appears to fail.

Let's tell the tester to choose Continue.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Fix extension order and numbering in UC04
commitResults.messageBody:
UC04 lists its extensions as 4a, 4b, 2a, 3a. The f/yes extension
happens at step 3 but is numbered 4b, and 2a gives no system
response.

Let's list the extensions in step order, renumber f/yes as 3b, add
TAssist's response to 2a, and say which kinds of records the prompt
names in step 4. 3a now matches the error, which names the student
ID and the group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let a student's weekly record be removed
commitResults.messageBody:
A student's attendance or participation for a week can be added or
replaced, but never removed. A week recorded by mistake therefore
cannot go back to Not recorded.

Let's add withoutRecord to WeeklyRecord, and withoutAttendanceRecord
and withoutParticipationRecord to Student. Like the other changes,
they return a copy and leave the original unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a command that clears a week's attendance
commitResults.messageBody:
A TA who marks the wrong week or student can change the mark to
present or absent, but cannot make the week Not recorded again. The
false mark then shows in attendance list and in group export.

Let's add AttendanceClearCommand, which removes one student's mark for
one week and shows the mark it removed. Clearing a week without a mark
changes nothing and says so, like re-entering the same mark.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a command that clears a week's participation
commitResults.messageBody:
A participation score entered for the wrong student or week can be
changed to another score, but not removed. Setting it to 0 is not a
fix either, because 0 is a real score.

Let's add ParticipationClearCommand, which removes one student's score
for one week and shows the score it removed. Clearing a week without a
score changes nothing and says so.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let users type attendance clear
commitResults.messageBody:
AttendanceClearCommand exists, but no command word reaches it and help
does not mention it.

Let's register attendance clear id/STUDENT_ID w/WEEK with a help entry
and an example, and document it in the User Guide. It takes only the
student and the week, so a status copied from attendance mark is
rejected rather than ignored.

The attendance list sample no longer relies on the state left by the
help examples, since the new example clears that mark.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let users type participation clear
commitResults.messageBody:
ParticipationClearCommand exists, but no command word reaches it and
help does not mention it.

Let's register participation clear id/STUDENT_ID w/WEEK with a help
entry and an example, and document it in the User Guide. The guide
points out that setting a score to 0 is not the same as clearing it.

Participation registration had no test of its own, so let's add one
that covers every participation command.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Explain how a weekly record is cleared
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide does not cover attendance clear and participation
clear, so developers cannot see how they work or why they are separate
commands.

Let's describe both commands and the model methods behind them, and
record why clear is its own subcommand rather than a special status or
an undo. UC05 and UC06 gain an extension for clearing a wrong record,
and the manual tests cover clearing, clearing twice, and a status
copied from attendance mark.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept s/o, d/o, a/l and a/p in student names
commitResults.messageBody:
Many legal names in Singapore and Malaysia contain s/o or d/o (son of,
daughter of), or a/l or a/p (the Malay equivalents). StudentName
rejects any slash, so these students cannot be entered as they appear
on the class list.

Let's accept these particles, in any case, when they stand alone
between two parts of a name. Other slashes are still rejected, and the
constraint message now mentions the particles.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let a command treat words like s/o as text
commitResults.messageBody:
The argument parser treats any word that starts with letters and a
slash as a prefix. In "n/Ravi s/o Kumar", s/o is therefore reported as
an unknown prefix s/, although it is part of the name.

Let's let a command declare literal words. A declared word that stands
alone between spaces stays in the value, ignoring case. Other commands
declare none, so their parsing is unchanged, and a literal word may not
start with one of the command's own prefixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let student add accept names with s/o or d/o
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding "Ravi s/o Kumar" fails with "Unknown prefix 's/'", which blames
a prefix the TA never meant to type.

Let's have student add declare s/o, d/o, a/l and a/p as literal words,
so they stay in the name, and mention them in its help and in the User
Guide. Other student commands still read every prefix as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Explain literal words such as s/o in names
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide says every prefix-like word is a parameter, which
is no longer true for the particles in student names.

Let's describe literal words, why student add declares only s/o, d/o,
a/l and a/p, and the alternatives we did not take. The manual tests now
cover adding names with these particles and the inputs still rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Hint to separate s/o when it is joined to a word
commitResults.messageBody:
A TA who types "n/Ravi s/oKumar" still sees only "Unknown prefix 's/'",
which does not say how to fix the name.

Let's add a hint to that error when the word starts with a literal
word: "If s/o is part of the value, put a space before and after it."
Other unknown prefixes keep the same message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find literal words with the same whitespace rule
commitResults.messageBody:
The literal word was cut at Character.isWhitespace, while the prefix
pattern splits words at \s. The two disagree on some Unicode spaces,
so a word could be read differently by the two steps.

Let's find the word with \S as well, so both steps see the same word.

commitResults.messageBody:
Register student find, display matching rows and counts, and let
student list restore the full roster. Distinguish an empty group
from a search with no matches, and open Students for both commands.

Update help and the guides to match the new behavior.

searches. Check that listing restores all students and restarting

through student list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test student query isolation and restoration

zero students reports a misleading search failure.

rows. Cover later additions and unchanged saved data with tests,
and document the behavior requested in the review of PR #148.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep active student filters visible in the UI

active, so the empty-state hint promises results that may stay hidden.

model and JavaFX regressions and guides for the review of PR #148.

commitResults.messageBody:
Add a command-box entry point that replaces the draft, returns focus,
and places the caret after the template without recording a command.

Reset history navigation for new drafts while retaining executed
commands. Cover failed input, repeated templates, focus, caret
placement, and history navigation before wiring student clicks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fill attendance templates from student row clicks
commitResults.messageBody:
Pass explicit clicks on populated student rows to the command box
through UI callbacks. Prepare an incomplete attendance command using
the row student ID and leave execution to Enter.

Verify focus, caret placement, unchanged data on clicks, validation
of incomplete input, and recording attendance after completion.
Document the shortcut and replacement of unfinished input.

commitResults.messageBody:

selection, and history navigation without changing saved records.

Verify current student IDs after group changes, deletion, filtering,
and sorting so templates cannot use a stale roster position. Add
manual acceptance checks for issue #68.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject trailing content after JSON values
commitResults.messageBody:
JSON loading accepts only the first value and silently ignores trailing
content. A later save can overwrite a malformed file without warning.

Reject content after the first value while allowing trailing whitespace,
and cover both string parsing and file loading with regression tests.

Refs #135

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify protection for malformed JSON files
commitResults.messageBody:
Appended content must trigger startup protection so later commands cannot
overwrite a malformed data file.

Extend startup and restart tests to cover trailing content, and verify
that trailing whitespace still permits loading and saving. Document the
single-object requirement and manual recovery checks.

Refs #135

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject duplicate week aliases when loading JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
Integer map keys discard conflicting aliases before validation can detect
them, so an unrelated save can silently remove a weekly record.

Check the original JSON keys before converting them to week numbers.
Reject duplicate aliases in participation and attendance while allowing
a single alias and records for distinct weeks.

Refs #134

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify file protection for duplicate week aliases
commitResults.messageBody:
Duplicate week aliases must activate startup protection before a command
can overwrite the original data file.

Cover protection through shutdown and restart for participation and
attendance, and verify that distinct weeks still load and save. Document
the duplicate rule and the steps for repairing affected files.

Refs #134

testing steps. Use the updated load-failure assertions from team master.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report actual submission changes for s/no
commitResults.messageBody:
Marking an unsubmitted assignment as not submitted claims a grade was
cleared even when no grade exists.

Leave already unsubmitted records unchanged and report that status.
Mention grade removal only when withdrawing a graded submission, and
cover missing records, repeated commands, and graded or ungraded work.

Refs #124

commitResults.messageTitle: Verify accurate submission feedback across restarts
commitResults.messageBody:
Repeated s/no commands should not change the saved file or imply that a
grade was removed. Real withdrawals must still persist their changes.

Cover unchanged records and graded or ungraded withdrawals through the
real command and storage path. Update the guides and manual checks to
match the feedback.

Refs #124

commitResults.messageTitle: Add undo and redo commands
commitResults.messageBody:
A TA who enters a wrong command, such as deleting the wrong student,
has no quick way to reverse it.

Let's add undo and redo for any command that changes and saves data.
LogicManager records the data from before each saved change, with the
command as entered, in a TAssistHistory kept by the model. Failed and
unchanged commands are not recorded, the restored data is saved, and
a failed save keeps both the data and the history as they were.

Up to 20 changes from the current session can be undone.
